story: According to Shona and Venda tradition, Mwari is the supreme creator deity, the author of all things and all life, in whom all things exist. Mwari is omnipotent and rules over all spirits. The same deity is called Inkhosi by the Northern and Southern Ndebele people. Reverence for Mwari dates back to the age of the ancient king Monomotapa, ruler of the Mutapa Kingdom on the Zambezi River. The first official recognition of Mwari came from the Kingdom of Zimbabwe, whose most notable ruler was Monomotapa. This worship was incorporated into the religious life of Great Zimbabwe. Mwari was frequently approached through spirit mediums at shrines located at Matonjeni in the Matopo Hills. Mwari is regarded as kind and loving, controlling not only creation but also land fertility and the rains that bring blessing. Mwari governs the forces of the Earth, including the fortune of journeys and social and political events. Though people sometimes prayed to Mwari alone, it was common to use spirit mediums as intermediaries. It was believed that no one had the right to call upon Mwari directly without first observing the proper protocol of expressing grievances or giving thanks through spirit mediums, who were possessed by ancestral and other spirits. In northern regions, Mwari was contacted through spirit mediums or spirits; in other regions, Mwari spoke to the people through an oracle. It was believed that anyone who defied this spiritual law and attempted to approach Mwari directly would develop leprosy, for the name of this holy, ineffable, and unknowable God was considered sacred and beyond all things.
